To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed two algorithms for stochastic training of GCNs with convergence guarantees and that our algorithms are empirically shown to converge faster and be more time efficient than previous neighbor sampling algorithms.
we develop a preprocessing method and two control variates based algorithms to reduce the receptive field of GCNs and guarantee their convergence to the local optimum.
we propose two new stochastic training algorithms for GCNs that have a similar convergence rate as the exact algorithm while using a much smaller receptive field size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions:
the convergence of GCN with a small receptive field size, which is an important problem in the application of GCN.
the following questions: How to reduce the receptive field of a graph convolutional neural network? How to train the network in an efficient way?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a theoretical analysis of the convergence of stochastic training for GCN.
this paper presents a novel method to train graph convolutional networks (GNNs) with a reduced computational cost.
our proposed algorithms are able to reduce the receptive field of a GCN by a significant factor, and the time complexity of training a GCN is reduced accordingly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first theoretical guarantee of neighbor sampling for GCNs and propose a new algorithm that is more practical.
we provide an efficient and theoretically justified algorithm for stochastic training of graph convolutional networks.
we propose a novel stochastic training method for GCNs, and it can significantly reduce the training time and memory usage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the receptive field size can be significantly reduced without hurting convergence speed, making GCN applicable to larger graphs.
stochastic training of GCNs can be much faster than previous neighbor sampling algorithms with the guarantee of convergence.
GCN can be efficiently trained with a small receptive field size per layer and a small number of neighbors per node.
